criteria.evidence: 17 files under apps/web/public/ - 16 JPEGs in mock/ and the wordmark SVG in brand/, per D7's split - and I proved the 'served locally, never the network' half end to end rather than reading it: the production build publishes all 17 under .output/public/, and against the nitro server on a free port each one returned 200 with the correct content-type and a body whose sha256 is byte-identical to the committed file, while a control path that is not in the dataset returned 404. Independently, a grep for http(s) URLs across apps/web/src and apps/web/public finds exactly two, neither a fetch of an image: the Google Fonts <link> in __root.tsx that R75 permits (Group 2's, not this group's) and the SVG namespace URI inside the mark. mock-data-assets.spec.ts makes the requirement mechanical for the six paths the dataset names, asserting each is root-relative and not remote and that each resolves to a committed file; I probed that guard by replacing a cover_url with https://images.example.com/lisboa.jpg and both its tests turned red, so it bites in both directions. On the 'only those the artboards reference' half I must be explicit about what I could and could not measure: the pencil MCP server failed to connect this session and the workspace holds no .qm wireframe, so I could not re-derive the 17 canvas ids from the artboards myself. What I could check corroborates the derivation exactly - all 17 files are distinct images (no two share a sha256, so nothing was downloaded twice under two names), every file is a real progressive JPEG or SVG at 900 px wide (160 px for the two avatars), nothing stray sits under public/, and the cell arithmetic closes with no slack: 7 login-collage cells + 7 Register-D mosaic cells + 4 covers + 2 avatars + 1 mark = 21 slots, and 21 - 17 = exactly the 4 overlaps the asset map names (familia-garcia and lisboa-2026 shared between the covers and the login collage, amigas-de-la-uni between the covers and the Register-D mosaic, photo-02 between the login collage and that mosaic). That arithmetic also settles the cross-check the coordinator's list got wrong: of Register-D's seven, five are exclusively its own. 11 of the 17 files are referenced by nothing in the repo yet because Groups 9 and 10 consume them, so for those the asset map in progress.md is the audit trail, not the code. Weight reported, not treated as a defect: 1,880,200 bytes (1.79 MiB) across 17 files, which I re-measured and which matches the Implementer's figure to the byte

findings.summary: the guard covers the 6 paths the dataset names (2 avatars + 4 covers) and therefore 6 of the 17 committed files. The 10 photo-NN.jpg and the wordmark are referenced by nothing in the repo until Groups 9, 10 and 7 consume them, so for 11 of 17 files nothing mechanical ties a committed byte to a used path - a file silently dropped, or an eleventh photo quietly added, would pass every gate. This is correct for this step rather than a defect, but it is the reason the asset map in progress.md is load-bearing for three later groups, and progress.md is archived at closeout. Worth the human knowing the map is the only audit trail for those 11 files. Advisory

passes.reason: owed by the per-step floor. The group adds no logic - 17 binaries plus the one spec file that guards them - so phases 3 and 4 have no surface: no TypeScript, no async, no error path, no teardown. Phase 1 and 2 reduce to the asset guard, which I probed red in both of its directions (a remote URL, and a path that resolves to no file). Naming is mechanical and deterministic as described, the two avatars are correctly 160 px rather than 900 px, and the one SVG is a real SVG. No file is a duplicate of another by content, which is the check that would have caught a careless download
